lesson.title: Domain and Range
intro: The domain of a function is the set of all possible input values, or x-values.
The range of a function is the set of all possible output values, or y-values.
When reading a graph, the domain describes how far the graph extends left and right, and the range describes how far it extends up and down.

example.problem: Find the domain and range of the function f(x) = x² + 3.
steps: Identify the type of function. This is a quadratic function.
The domain of a quadratic function is all real numbers.
Since x² is always nonnegative, the minimum value occurs when x = 0.
So the smallest output is 3, and all larger outputs are possible.
example.answer: Domain: all real numbers. Range: y ≥ 3.

questions.explanation: The absolute value expression has a minimum of 0, so the smallest value of the function is −5.

questions.prompt: Which function has a domain of all real numbers and a range greater than or equal to three?
questions.explanation: Since x² ≥ 0 for all real x, x² + 3 ≥ 3. Its domain is all real numbers and its range is y ≥ 3.

questions.prompt: A function is graphed on the set of axes below. The domain of this function is
questions.explanation: The graph begins at x = −2 with a closed point, so −2 is included in the domain.

questions.prompt: The graph of f(x) is shown below. The domain of this function is
questions.explanation: The graph starts at an open point at x = 0 and ends at a closed point at x = 12, so the domain is 0 < x ≤ 12.
